subject: chemistry

moments.title: Goodyear's vulcanisation
moments.body: Goodyear accidentally drops rubber mixed with sulphur onto a hot stove. The product is stable — vulcanised rubber. He dies in debt; the company that bears his name comes later.
moments.takeaway: The first synthetic modification of a natural polymer — by accident.

moments.title: Bakelite
moments.body: Baekeland synthesises a phenol-formaldehyde resin that can be moulded. Bakelite — the first fully synthetic plastic — launches the plastics age.
moments.takeaway: The first fully synthetic plastic. The plastic age begins.

moments.title: Staudinger and macromolecules
moments.body: Staudinger proposes that polymers are giant covalent molecules. Chemists ridicule the idea: 'Dear colleague, leave the concept of large molecules well alone... no such things as macromolecules exist.' He wins the 1953 Nobel anyway.
moments.takeaway: Staudinger fights for the idea that polymers are real molecules — for 30 years.

moments.title: Nylon
moments.body: Carothers, leading DuPont's industrial research, develops nylon, neoprene and other synthetic polymers. He suffers depression and dies by suicide in 1937, before nylon is launched (1939).
moments.takeaway: Modern synthetic polymers are born in industrial labs.

moments.title: Ziegler-Natta catalysis
moments.body: Ziegler and Natta develop catalysts (now called Ziegler-Natta) for controlled polymerisation of olefins. They enable polyethylene, polypropylene and isotactic polymers. 1963 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Polymer chemistry becomes a multi-trillion-dollar industry.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: Plastics production is ~400 million tonnes per year. Microplastics are found in every ocean, every continent, in human blood. Biodegradable plastics are a major research field.
now.open_questions: Can biodegradable polymers replace conventional plastics at scale? How do microplastics affect health?

reflection: Staudinger was mocked for the idea of macromolecules; Carothers, who built modern polymer chemistry, killed himself. Why has plastic's success come at such cost?
